verify.lens: Skeptic: facts, sources, legal limits and whether it can be built on the current repo (interactive-tools branch, 22 Sep 2026). The spec's statistics hold up: FTC more than 5x (reports filed in 2021), FTC task-scam alert of 14 Aug 2025 ($5 to $20 payouts, then a crypto deposit), Europol more than 90%, EBF names ages 18 to 34 and students, 27 lakh mule accounts (Rajya Sabha, 11 Mar 2026), IRS hiring page updated 18 Feb 2026, and SEC HoweyTrade exists. What fails is the content and the mechanism.
problems: Out-of-date lesson reference. The India money-mule lesson has no 'Sunrise Tutorials' screen any more. Screen d2 is now from 'Tutoring centre office'; the name was removed in commit 2dcb4ce and appears nowhere in src. The spec's defaults, its ordinary list and its effort line all mark 'Sunrise Tutorials' as ordinary: true, so a builder either finds nothing to mark or puts the name back. It is also a common real business name in India, which is an impersonation risk.

The closing line 'Every situation you answered comes back for review in a day or two' is false. schedule() in src/lib/progress.ts moves a right answer up one Leitner box (1, 3, 7, 14, 30 days). The three lesson screens keep their lesson ids, so a reader who already answered them in the lesson gets 3 to 30 days. Answering the same check twice in one day also moves it from box 1 to box 2 with no spacing between the two answers, which corrupts the review schedule. spot-the-fake has the same flaw today.

The India ordinary case teaches readers to send identity and bank details by message. In 'internship-offer' the right answer is 'accept and send the details' to a message from 'HR, the firm where you interviewed' asking for 'your PAN and account details before joining'. That sender label is exactly what a fake offer letter claims. The EU and US ordinary cases hand details over in person on day one. 'TDS as applicable' adds an acronym and a tax claim that a stipend of ₹1.44 lakh a year usually does not trigger as salary TDS.

The reveal rule and the reflection don't fit most screens. Every reveal must name 'whose money would pass through the reader's account' and say that 'moving it can be a crime', and the reflection asks 'whose money would have passed through your account?'. Yet 5 of the 12 scam screens (premium-tasks, joining-kit, the US task-pay deposit, text-interview, the US parcel reshipping) put the reader's own money, details or name at risk, not other people's money in their account. The 6 ordinary screens don't fit either. Telling a task-scam or fee-scam victim that moving money can be a crime is wrong and blames the reader.

India's two new patterns have no Indian source. No India lesson teaches premium-tasks (a task scam) or joining-kit (a fee before work); the linked lesson is about mules. The only India source listed is the cybercrime.gov.in brochure, an image PDF whose text I could not extract to confirm it covers either pattern. The task-scam reasoning rests on a US FTC alert.

The India reporting route doesn't fit a drill, and the strings are not copies. 1930 is the helpline for financial cyber fraud, meaning money already lost; most screens are an approach with nothing lost. The spec says reportTo is 'copied from each edition's lesson', but the IN, EU and US strings are paraphrases, not the lessons' labels.
The US route drops the lesson's instruction 'Report every job scam, even one that cost you nothing'. In a drill, the case where nothing was lost is the common one.

The EU apprenticeship answer 'read the contract, then sign' ignores age. Readers of 15 to 17 generally need a parent or guardian to consent to or co-sign an apprenticeship contract, and the rule differs by member state (for example, Germany's BBiG §11 has the contract handed to the minor's legal representatives). The spec does not say the rule varies. 'Kovač Bakery' is a real, common surname plus a trade and is likely to match real bakeries, which breaks the 'never a real employer' rule.

The US campus job's 'Bring ID for Form I-9 on your first day' is imprecise. USCIS lets the employee choose documents from List A, or from List B plus List C, and present them within three business days of starting. An employer may not specify which documents, and ID alone (List B) is not enough.

The 'new' screens repeat the lessons. US 'fake-check' reuses the lesson's own document and worked example ($2,850 check, keep $300, the rest to a vendor). EU 'payment-agent' reuses the EU lesson's document (receive client payments, forward them, take a percentage, send your IBAN). Both test memory of the example, not the ability to tell cases apart.

The spec treats unbuilt pieces as existing. The repo has no src/content/drills/, no fromLesson, no bank reportTo, no tests/unit/drills.test.ts and no impersonation 'denylist test'; tests/unit/lessons.test.ts only bans hype words. Today [tool].astro hard-codes slug === 'spot-the-fake' with lessons.find(a drill with reportTo). Drill.astro makes every id `${lessonId}#d${index+1}`, so mixed ids cannot happen. checks.json.ts emits only lesson checks. The scenario schema has no ordinary field. ToolMeta has no kind; a tool reads 'Practice' only when regions is set, otherwise it reads 'Calculator'. The drill page also prints 'The numbers it opens with are an example, not a prediction', which makes no sense for a drill.

The options and 'why' text are left to the builder ('The builder writes 2–3 options with a why for each'). The whys are where the claims about crime and liability, and the risk of blaming the reader, sit. Text nobody has reviewed cannot pass the content-reviewer gate.

SSN appears in the US text-interview answer and cue, but there is no glossary term for it (pan, tds, iban, form-i-9, w-4, task-scam and fake-check exist). Bank screens get no Term popovers, and nothing tests acronyms in the bank.

The FTC evidence is out of date and incomplete. The '5x' figure comes from reports filed in 2021 and the spec does not date it that way. A newer FTC data spotlight (Dec 2024, 'Paying to get paid') supports the task screens directly: task scams went from 0.6% of job-scam reports in 2021 to 38.8% in the first half of 2024. The FTC alert of 30 Apr 2026 (unexpected job texts; never pay to get paid) backs text-interview but is not in the spec's sources.

The 27 lakh wording is imprecise. The source says 'over 27 lakh mule accounts have been shared with the participating entities of Suspect Registry', not 'India has shared ... through its Suspect Registry'.
joining-kit has no amount, although the ₹1,499 fee is what the reader should see. MockScreen shows the large figure only when amount is set, and premium-tasks does set it.
fixes: Replace every 'Sunrise Tutorials' with 'the tutoring centre screen (in/protect-your-money/money-mule#d2, from "Tutoring centre office")'. Mark ordinary lesson screens by check id (in/...#d2, eu/credit-and-fraud/money-mule#d2, us/how-business-works/job-scam#d2), never by firm name.

Change the closing line to: 'Every situation you answered joins your review. One you missed comes back tomorrow; one you got right comes back later each time.' In src/lib/progress.ts schedule(): if the item already exists and its due date is after today, return progress with its box and due date unchanged, because answering early is not a spaced retrieval. Add a unit test: answering twice on the same day leaves box 1 and a due date of tomorrow.

Rewrite 'internship-offer' to these lines: 'Offer letter attached: stipend ₹12,000 a month.' / 'Paid into your bank account on the 7th, from the firm's own account.' / 'Bring your PAN card and bank details to the office on your joining day.' Action: 'Accept offer'. Q: 'You had two interviews at their office last month, and the letter matches what they told you.' Answer: 'Accept, and hand over the details at the office on your joining day.' Cue: 'You met them in person, your details go in person, and money flows from the employer to you.' Drop 'TDS as applicable'.

Change the reveal rule to: 'Each reveal names the sign and which way the money or your details would move: in to you from an employer, out of you to a stranger, or through your account for someone else. Only screens where other people's money passes through the reader's account (IN Karan and Arjun; EU Dario, Alex, payment-agent and account-for-hire) may say that moving it can be a crime, and never call the reader a criminal.' Change the reflection to: 'Which message were you least sure of, and which way would the money have moved?'

Add Indian sources for the two new India screens and base their whys on them: the MHA Year End Review 2023 (PIB, https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1991936), where I4C's NCTAU identified over 100 websites running organised investment and task-based part-time job frauds, blocked by MeitY; and the DoT Chakshu facility (https://sancharsaathi.gov.in/sfc/), which takes reports of suspected fraud communications, including online job offers. Both returned 403 to my fetch, so open both before publishing. If no Indian source can be found for joining-kit, replace that screen.

Don't copy strings: the bank's reportTo is the fromLesson's reportTo object, used as-is. If India needs a drill-specific line, use: 'If money has moved, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in straight away. If you only got the message, report it through Chakshu at sancharsaathi.gov.in. Keep the messages, account details and dates.' Check Chakshu's current wording first.
US reportTo: use the lesson's label as written: 'If you deposited a check or sent money, tell your bank straight away. Report every job scam, even one that cost you nothing, at reportfraud.ftc.gov.'

EU apprenticeship: change the sender to 'The bakery where you did a trial shift' (no real surname). Answer: 'Read the contract and sign it. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian usually signs or agrees too; the rule depends on your country.' Keep the cue as it is.

US campus-job: change the line to 'Bring documents for Form I-9 in your first three days of work. You choose which, from the list on the form.' Answer: 'Accept, and bring the documents.' Source: USCIS, Completing Section 2 (https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/completing-form-i-9/completing-section-2-employer-review-and-attestation).

Rewrite US 'fake-check' with new numbers and a new story, for example from 'Hiring team, harborlineevents.example': 'You're hired as a personal assistant.' / 'We mailed you a check for $3,160.' / 'Keep $260 and pay the rest to our event supplier through a payment app.' Rewrite EU 'payment-agent' as a different mule variant, for example 'Crypto exchange assistant: buy crypto with client money that lands in your account and send it to our wallet; keep 7%.' Same answer shape: refuse, because your account is the job.

Set the effort to 'depends on the drill-bank spec landing first' and list the files it must change: [tool].astro (map tool slug to fromLesson plus bank instead of slug === 'spot-the-fake'); Drill.astro (take an explicit checkId per scenario); checks.json.ts (emit bank ids with lesson = the tool title and lessonPath = `${region}/tools/job-offer-check`, without emitting lesson screens twice); schema.ts (optional ordinary: boolean on a drill scenario); tools.ts (set regions: ['in','eu','us'] explicitly or add kind: 'drill'); hide the 'numbers it opens with' note on drill pages. Write tests/unit/drills.test.ts plus a denylist test of real bank, app, employer and regulator names before claiming impersonation is 'checked by the denylist test'.

Write every option and why for all 9 new scenarios in the spec: 2 or 3 options each, every why 25 words or fewer, with the right answer's why naming the sign. Run content-reviewer on the three JSON files before building. drills.test.ts applies the lessons.test.ts rules to bank text: banned words, 30-word sentence cap, no exclamation marks, and every acronym spelled out or a glossary term.
Spell out 'Social Security number' everywhere in the US bank, or add a social-security-number glossary term. Enforce it with the acronym rule in drills.test.ts.

In whyItHelps, write the FTC line as '(FTC data spotlight, Dec 2022, reports filed in 2021)'. Add https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/data-visualizations/data-spotlight/2024/12/paying-get-paid-gamified-job-scams-drive-record-losses as the task-scam source, and https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2026/04/job-offer-text-probably-scam as the text-interview source.
Reword to: 'Over 27 lakh mule accounts have been shared with the entities taking part in India's Suspect Registry (Minister of State for Home Affairs, Rajya Sabha, 11 March 2026).'

build.title: Rent and bills as a share of net pay
build.answers: How much of my net pay would this room take?
build.short: How much of my pay goes on rent?
build.intro: Answers one question: rent and bills together, what share of your net pay do they take?

inputs.label: Net pay a month
inputs.hint: What reaches your account. If you receive a housing allowance, take it off the rent instead.

inputs.label: Rent a month (your share)
inputs.hint: The price in the listing or contract. Weekly rent: multiply by 52 and divide by 12.

inputs.label: Bills a month
inputs.hint: Water, power, gas and heating. In a flat share, your share; ask the current tenants.

inputs.label: Deposit, in months of rent
inputs.hint: Returned at the end if nothing is owed. Rules on its size are national. For a deposit given as an amount, divide it by the rent.

inputs.label: First month paid in advance (a select: yes or no)
Moving and connecting the bills
Saved so far
inputs.hint: What you could use on day one without borrowing.

outputs: Headline (Figure): 53.3%, 'of net pay on rent and bills'.
Ledger: Net pay €1,125; − Rent €520; = After rent €605; − Bills €80; double-ruled Left after housing €525.
Fact: Eurostat's 40% line on this pay is €450; rent and bills are €150 above it.
Ledger, day one: Deposit, 2 months' rent, €1,040; + First month in advance €520; + Moving and connecting the bills €140; double-ruled Day one €1,700.
Fact: day one takes €500 more than the €1,200 saved (or 'covered, with €X left before the first payday').
Note: Eurostat measures household disposable income; here, as in the lesson, it is set against one person's net pay.
How this is worked out: the line is a statistic, not a rule, plus the lesson's 'pay nothing before a viewing' with the European Consumer Centres route.
build.resultSentence: Rent and bills of {housing} take {share}% of your {netPay} net pay and leave {left}. Eurostat's 40% line on this pay is {line}, and these costs are {gap} {above|below} it. Moving in takes {dayOne} before the first payday, {dayOneGap} {more than|less than} the {saved} saved. Example: Rent and bills of €600 take 53.3% of your €1,125 net pay and leave €525. Eurostat's 40% line on this pay is €450, and these costs are €150 above it. Moving in takes €1,700 before the first payday, €500 more than the €1,200 saved.
build.maths: housingShare(netPay, rent, bills, linePercent): { housing, share: number | null, left, line, gap }. housing = round2(rent + bills); share = round1(housing / netPay × 100) when netPay > 0; left = round2(netPay − housing); line = round2(netPay × linePercent / 100); gap = round2(housing − line). dayOneCost(rent, depositMonths, firstMonthUpfront: boolean, moveCosts, saved): { deposit, total, gap }. deposit = round2(rent × depositMonths); total = round2(deposit + (firstMonthUpfront ? rent : 0) + moveCosts); gap = round2(total − saved), positive when day one needs more than is saved. linePercent = 40 is a Rule in regions.ts (Eurostat housing-cost overburden glossary, with asOf). Pins: 1,125 / 520 / 80 gives housing 600, 53.3%, 525 left, a 450 line and +150. Day one: 2 × 520 + 520 + 140 = 1,700, gap +500 against 1,200. The lesson's practice figures: 1,240 / 430 / 70 gives a 496 line and +4; 1,400 / 480 / 70 gives a 560 line and −10.
edgeCases: Net pay of 0 or blank: error text under the field.
Rent and bills above net pay: 'left' is negative, shown in the loss style, and the sentence says rent and bills are more than the pay.
A housing allowance: taken off the rent (see the hint), matching Eurostat's 'net of housing allowances'.
Weekly rent: × 52 ÷ 12 (see the hint), never × 4.
Countries outside the euro: the currency select changes the currency, and the sum works in złoty or kronor.
The 40% is Eurostat's statistical measure for households, not a rule or an approval, and How this is worked out says so.
Deposit rules are national: covered by the hint and How this is worked out.
Saved at or above day one: 'covered, with {x} left before the first payday'.
build.whyItHelps: The moving-out lesson teaches exactly this test, on a €520 room with €80 of bills and a Friday deadline. Eurostat reports that 9.7% of 15–29-year-olds lived in an overburdened household in 2024, and that young people leave home at 26.2 on average (the lesson's sources). The research sweep found youth budget simulators on French and Dutch public sites, but none that sets rent against a sourced line. The lesson's explorer offers only three fixed pay levels, and the tool it names (the budget planner) is never linked, because a deduction explorable renders no tool link.
build.modelledOn: The French government's student budget simulator (one-off moving costs counted separately, reference figures with a named source) and Nibud's running monthly total. What is different: a few numbers and one share instead of a questionnaire. The line is Eurostat's EU-wide definition with its source and date, no national aid schemes are named, and there are no trackers or emoji.
risks: Verdict framing: the 40% is described as Eurostat's statistic, never a pass mark. The day-one sentence says 'more than the amount saved', not 'short' (the content-legal judge on proposal 2's wording).
Proxy measure: a note says household disposable income is replaced here by one person's net pay, as in the lesson.
Rental fraud at the same moment: How this is worked out keeps 'pay nothing before a viewing' with the ECC route.
Europe only: India has no official line, the US line (HUD's 30%) is measured on gross income, and neither edition has a lesson on it (both judges).
build.effort: small: src/lib/finance.ts (housingShare, dayOneCost) + tests; src/islands/RentShare.tsx (about 100 lines, about 2–3 KB gz); src/lib/regions.ts (eu rentShare with the 40% Rule); src/lib/tools.ts (regions ['eu']); [tool].astro; e2e; frontmatter: eu/moving-out (tool: rent-share, moreTools: [budget]).

verify.lens: Skeptic, safety and scope: advice or verdict framing, named products, personal data, moralising, content rules, maths edge cases, and whether the build plan works against the real code
problems: The currency edge case is false. src/lib/format.ts LOCALES holds only INR, USD, GBP, EUR, BRL and NGN, with no PLN, SEK, CZK, HUF, DKK or RON, so the currency select cannot give a result 'in złoty or kronor'. regions.ts (eu problems) already says 'The calculators here work in euros; the ideas work in any currency', which contradicts the spec.

The lesson link will not render. In src/layouts/LessonLayout.astro (the deduction branch, around line 332) DeductionExplorer gets no toolHref, so setting `tool: rent-share` on eu/money-basics/moving-out still shows no link. `moreTools` is not in src/content/schema.ts, and the lesson schema is not .strict(), so zod drops the key without an error. Changing `tool: budget` to `rent-share` also removes moving-out from /eu/tools/budget under 'Lessons that use this', because [tool].astro filters on `l.data.tool === tool.slug`.

[tool].astro treats any tool limited to some editions as the drill. It sets `kind={tool.regions ? 'Practice' : 'Calculator'}`, which goes into the Pagefind meta, so rent-share would be indexed as 'Practice'. The `scenario` map has no rent-share entry, so the page loses its 'It opens on an example' line, which breaks the rule that every tool opens on an edition example. The meta description on src/pages/[region]/tools/index.astro hard-codes the five calculator names.

The maths refers to helpers that do not exist. regions.ts has no `Rule` type and no `asOf` field. finance.ts has no round1 or round2; the only round2 is private to src/lib/lesson-math.ts (line 193). ToolDefaults has no rentShare slot, and it must be optional because only eu has one.

Negative inputs are not handled. toolkit toNumber('-520') returns -520, and NumberField's min="0" is only an HTML hint, so a negative rent, bills, depositMonths, moveCosts or saved gives a negative housing cost, share or deposit. For net pay the spec only covers 0 or blank, not negative values.

At net pay ≤ 0, housingShare returns share: null, but resultSentence still fills '{share}%' and prints a €0 line and gap. The spec gives no replacement sentence and does not say which Figure or Facts to hide.

Being exactly on the line is not handled. The sentence has only '{above|below}', so gap = 0 prints '€0 above it'. Eurostat's glossary counts only 'more than 40%', so exactly 40% is not overburdened. Rounding also clashes: housing 450.01 on 1,125 shows '40.0%' next to '€0.01 above it'. The spec does not say whether above or below is decided on rounded or unrounded values.

The day-one wording is specified twice and the two versions disagree. resultSentence uses '{dayOneGap} {more than|less than} the {saved} saved', while the outputs Fact uses 'covered, with {x} left'. A gap of exactly 0 has no wording.

Deposit in months is lossy and breaks in some cases. The hint's 'divide the amount by the rent' gives repeating decimals: 1,000 ÷ 520 = 1.923…, and typing 1.92 gives a €998.40 deposit, not €1,000. It cannot work at rent 0. The label pluralises badly ('1 months' rent', '0 months' rent', '1.923 months' rent'). Where a deposit is set on base or cold rent, months × all-in rent overstates it.

Charges can be counted twice. Many EU listings quote rent with some bills or charges already included (heating or water in service charges, 'warm' rent, 'charges comprises'). A reader who follows 'the price in the listing' and then adds heating and water under Bills counts them twice. The Bills hint also leaves out charges Eurostat counts as housing cost, such as refuse removal.

The housing-allowance hint covers only half of Eurostat's rule. Eurostat (glossary, checked) nets housing allowances out of both housing costs and disposable income. The net-pay hint says 'what reaches your account', which includes an allowance paid to the reader, and does not say to leave it out of net pay.

Attribution: 'Eurostat's 40% line on this pay is €450' credits Eurostat with a figure it never computes. Its measure uses household disposable income net of allowances, not one person's net pay. A note further down does not fix a label that misattributes the number.

Verdict styling is unspecified. Only a negative 'left' is given loss style. If the implementer also colours the 40%-line gap or the day-one gap as a loss, a statistic becomes a pass/fail mark, which is the verdict framing the spec says it avoids.
`short` is 'How much of my pay goes on rent?'. It drops bills, which is exactly the rent-only mistake the lesson's document question and first quiz check train readers out of.

Percent formatting has a trap. format.ts percent() expects a fraction (0.533) and formats it through Intl, while the spec's share is already ×100 (53.3), so passing it straight in prints 5,330%. Adding '%' by hand to a number skips locale formatting.

The select can take bad values from a link. readQuery accepts any string of 24 characters or fewer, so ?firstMonthUpfront=evil reaches the select, and the spec does not say how unknown values are read. The kit's early-typing adoption also needs the id `${prefix}-firstMonthUpfront`.

Privacy: ToolActions' 'Copy link' puts netPay and saved in the query string. Anyone who opens the link sends the reader's pay and savings to the host (GitHub Pages) in the request, which cuts against 'nothing typed leaves the browser' for the most personal figures any calculator asks for.

depositMonths = 0 prints a '0 months' rent, €0' row. The moveCosts, firstMonthUpfront and saved fields have no hint (saved does have one; moveCosts has none), so readers do not know whether to include connection fees or furniture.
fixes: Either add { code: 'pl-PL', currency: 'PLN', label: 'Poland (zł)' }, { code: 'sv-SE', currency: 'SEK', label: 'Sweden (kr)' }, { code: 'cs-CZ', currency: 'CZK', label: 'Czechia (Kč)' }, { code: 'hu-HU', currency: 'HUF', label: 'Hungary (Ft)' }, { code: 'da-DK', currency: 'DKK', label: 'Denmark (kr)' } and { code: 'ro-RO', currency: 'RON', label: 'Romania (lei)' } to LOCALES in src/lib/format.ts, with a format.test.ts case for each (this changes every calculator), or replace the edge case with: 'The tool works in euros and the currencies in the select; the same sum works in złoty or kronor by hand.'

In LessonLayout.astro pass `toolHref={d.tool ? `${prefix}/tools/${d.tool}` : undefined}` to DeductionExplorer, and render the existing 'try it' tool link in DeductionExplorer.tsx when toolHref is set. build.title: Tax on side income and fees
build.answers: How much tax is still to pay, or to come back, on what my work brought in?
build.short: What tax is left on my side income?
build.intro: Answers one question: after what was already taken or paid, how much tax is left to pay, or comes back?

inputs.label: Fees invoiced this year
Paid into your account
inputs.hint: The gap is tax the payer deducted in your name. Your Annual Information Statement shows it.

inputs.label: Tax due on the year (from your return or the department's calculator)
inputs.hint: Worked out on the whole year's income. This tool never works it out. On the lesson's ₹1,50,000 it is ₹0.

inputs.label: Deducted but not yet on your statement
inputs.hint: A payer that has not filed yet. It follows once the payer corrects its filing.

inputs.label: Money in from the work this year
inputs.hint: Tutoring, gigs and sales, before any fees. It counts whether or not a 1099-K arrives.

inputs.label: Costs of the work
inputs.hint: Shipping, packaging, platform fees: only what your records show.

inputs.label: Income tax to set aside, % of profit (an example)
inputs.hint: Yours depends on the whole year's income and may be nil. 10% is the lesson's example; the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator or your return gives a real figure.

inputs.label: Already paid or withheld this year

outputs: India headline (Figure): ₹15,000, 'comes back when you file the year's return' (or '{x} still to pay' when tax due is larger).

India ledger (the lesson's own worked ledger): Fees invoiced ₹1,50,000; − Paid into your account ₹1,35,000; = Tax withheld in your name ₹15,000; − Tax due on the year ₹0; = Refund due for the year ₹15,000; − Deducted but not yet on your statement ₹0; double-ruled Comes back on this return ₹15,000.
India fact: a statement records credits; only a return works out a refund.
US headline (Figure): $1,207, 'still to pay for the year'.

US ledger: Money in $6,000; − Costs of the work $1,000; = Net profit $5,000; Self-employment tax, 15.3% of $4,618 (92.35% of profit), $707; + Income tax at your example 10%, $500; = Tax for the year $1,207; − Already paid or withheld $0; double-ruled Still to pay $1,207.
US fact: 24.1% of profit and 20.1% of money in; self-employment tax alone is 14.1% of profit.
US fact, shown when still to pay is $1,000 or more: the IRS generally expects payments during the year from people who will owe $1,000 or more, on 15 April, 15 June, 15 September and 15 January.
US 'Rules as of' line: 92.35%, 15.3%, the $400 test and the $1,000 line, each linked to its IRS page with a date.
build.resultSentence: India: Of {invoiced} invoiced, {withheld} was taken as tax in your name. With {taxDue} due on the year, {refund} comes back when you file the year's return. US: Of {moneyIn} in, {profit} is profit after costs. Tax on it comes to {tax}: {seTax} of self-employment tax, set by law, and {incomeTax} at your example {rate}%, so {stillToPay} is still to pay. Examples: 'Of ₹1,50,000 invoiced, ₹15,000 was taken as tax in your name. With ₹0 due on the year, ₹15,000 comes back when you file the year's return.' 'Of $6,000 in, $5,000 is profit after costs. Tax on it comes to $1,207: $707 of self-employment tax, set by law, and $500 at your example 10%, so $1,207 is still to pay.'
build.maths: India: tdsRefundLines(invoiced, arrived, taxDue, missing) returns the existing deductions(invoiced, [{ label: 'Paid into your account', amount: arrived, subtotalLabel: 'Tax withheld in your name' }, { label: 'Tax due on the year', amount: taxDue, subtotalLabel: 'Refund due for the year' }, { label: 'Deducted but not yet on your statement', amount: missing }]). A net above 0 comes back; a net below 0 is still to pay (−net). No rate is held. US: selfEmploymentSetAside(moneyIn, costs, incomeTaxPercent, alreadyPaid, rules): profit = max(0, round2(moneyIn − costs)). applies = profit × 92.35 / 100 ≥ 400: the IRS test on net earnings, taken unrounded, so it starts at a profit of $433.14. counted = applies ? Math.round(profit × 0.9235 + 1e-9) : 0; seTax = applies ? Math.round(counted × 0.153 + 1e-9) : 0. Both are whole dollars, as Schedule SE allows, matching the lesson's $4,618 and $707. incomeTax = round2(profit × incomeTaxPercent / 100); tax = seTax + incomeTax; balance = round2(tax − alreadyPaid), negative when more than enough is paid. shareOfProfit = round1(tax / profit × 100); shareOfMoneyIn = round1(tax / moneyIn × 100). 92.35, 15.3, 400 and 1,000 are Rules in regions.ts (the IRS self-employment tax and estimated taxes pages, with asOf). Pins: US 6,000 / 1,000 / 10 / 0 gives profit 5,000, counted 4,618, SE 707 (the lesson's $707), income tax 500, tax 1,207, 24.1% and 20.1%. Profits of 3,000 and 8,000 give SE 424 and 1,130 (the lesson's practice answers). A profit of 433.13 gives SE 0; 434 gives SE 61. India 1,50,000 / 1,35,000 / 0 / 0 gives 15,000 back; 2,40,000 / 2,16,000 / 0 / 6,000 gives 18,000 back (the lesson's practice).
edgeCases: US costs above money in: profit is 0, and the sentence says the work made a loss on these figures, so no tax is worked out on it.
US profit under $433.14: no self-employment tax. Income tax may still apply, and the sentence says so.

US: the deduction for half of self-employment tax and the standard deduction are not modelled, so the income tax line can overstate. The assumption line says so, and How this is worked out links the IRS estimated taxes page and the Tax Withholding Estimator.
US state income tax is not included: stated, with a link to usa.gov/state-taxes.
More already paid than the tax worked out here: 'more has been paid than this sum shows; the year's return settles it'.
India: tax due above what was withheld gives the 'still to pay' sentence. No slabs, regimes or presumptive taxation are modelled, and How this is worked out links incometax.gov.in.
India: arrived above invoiced, or missing above withheld: error text asking to check the statement.
A rate above 100: error text.
build.whyItHelps: REGIONAL_TEACHING names US self-employment tax as tax that arrives late (15.3% once net earnings reach $400) and lists a side-hustle tax set-aside as US format 5. The IRS says gig income is reportable with or without a 1099-K. In India, the tds-refund lesson's intern had ₹15,000 withheld on an income that owed nothing, and only a return brings it back. Today se-tax links the budget planner and tds-refund links side-hustle profit; neither tool does this sum. The India sweep found the search for it leads to regime verdicts (CalcWise), consultation pushes (1 Finance) and 'Hire a CA' (ClearTax).
build.modelledOn: The se-tax lesson's split and the tds-refund lesson's deduction ledger; CalcWise's eligibility gate with its reason; the IRS estimated taxes page for the $1,000 line and the four dates. What is different: the only rates held are US constants set in law. India computes no tax at all, because the reader types what is due. There is no regime choice, no deductions menu and no filing funnel.

This is the content-legal judge's fix: proposal 0's flat example rate on profit contradicted the tds-refund quiz ('Each band's rate applies only inside the band'). The US income tax share is the lesson's labelled example. Each edition links its official route.

The judges differed: the engineering judge ranked this tool 7th, the content-legal judge last. It is built last, with the content-legal fixes, and needs the content-reviewer's sign-off (engineering judge).

problems: US default headline is wrong for the reader it opens on. The 10% income-tax default turns the lesson's $5,000 profit into '$1,207 still to pay for the year'. Under 2026 rules (IRS release of 9 Oct 2025, irs.gov/node/151941), the single standard deduction is $16,100, and a dependent's is the greater of $1,350 or earned income + $450. A 15–21-year-old whose only income is this $5,000 owes $0 federal income tax, so the true federal figure is $707. The spec rejected a flat rate on profit for India because it contradicts the tds-refund quiz's point that each band's rate applies only inside the band. The US flat 10% on profit makes the same band error: the 10% bracket starts only after the standard deduction, and runs to $12,400 of taxable income in 2026. It also sets the 24.1% / 20.1% 'facts'.

The same default wrongly shows the $1,000 estimated-tax fact. $1,207 passes the $1,000 line, so the tool tells the default reader that the IRS expects quarterly payments. On real 2026 figures, that reader's tax is $707, under the line.

The estimated-tax fact leaves out the exception that fits this audience best. The IRS estimated taxes page (reviewed 28 Jun 2026) says no estimated tax is required if you had no tax liability for the prior year, were a US citizen or resident for the whole year, and that year covered 12 months. Most 15–21-year-olds with a first side income meet all three. The page also sets the $1,000 test after withholding and credits, and offers the 90% current-year and 100% prior-year safe harbours. The spec states only '$1,000 or more → four dates'.

No Social Security wage base cap. The 12.4% part applies only up to the yearly maximum: $184,500 for 2026, $176,100 for 2025 per the 2025 Schedule SE instructions. The 2.9% part is uncapped, and 0.9% Additional Medicare tax applies above $200,000 for single filers. As specified, $300,000 of profit gives $42,389 of SE tax; the correct figure is about $31,600. The IRS SE-tax page the spec plans to cite is stale here: it still quotes the 2024 base of $168,600. The 2026 base was confirmed from search results pointing to the SSA FAQ (KA-02387) and several secondary sources; ssa.gov returned 403 to a direct fetch.

The source for the $400 test is wrong. Topic 554 and the SE-tax page both say '$400 or more of net earnings from self-employment'. Topic 554 applies 92.35% to 'your net earnings', which reads as a test on profit before the multiplier. Only the Schedule SE instructions put the test after 92.35% (line 4c ≥ $400). Those are the 2025 instructions; the 2026 ones are not out yet. Citing the SE-tax page or Topic 554 for the 92.35%-based test cites a page that says something else.

The threshold rounding is inconsistent. `applies` is tested on the unrounded profit × 0.9235, but `counted` is rounded to whole dollars 'as Schedule SE allows'. A whole-dollar filer with $433 of profit rounds line 4a to $400, meets the ≥$400 test and owes $61; the pin says $433.13 gives $0. The spec's '$433.14' start point is precise to the cent only under one of two allowed conventions.

US 'Already paid or withheld this year' invites double counting. A reader with a W-2 job will type the job's withholding, which already pays the job's own tax. Here it is set against tax on the side income only, so what is left is understated.

US 'still to pay' presents an example-rate estimate as a liability. The income-tax part is an example rate and the half-SE-tax deduction is ignored, so the figure is a set-aside estimate, not an amount owed.

Lesson and glossary fixes are incomplete. The spec corrects only the se-tax summary. The net-earnings glossary still defines net earnings as net profit ('what came in, minus business expenses'). The se-tax body (line 184: 'Your net earnings are your net profit… Once they reach $400'), keyIdea, details line 108, the self-employment-tax glossary and REGIONAL_TEACHING ('15.3% SE tax over $400') all still put the test on profit. The tool and the lesson would then contradict each other. Separately, the Schedule SE instructions exclude newspaper sales income for under-18s, so 'whatever your age' is not unconditional.

India derives the tax credit from invoiced minus arrived. That gap can also be GST billed, platform or gateway fees, currency conversion (foreign clients have no TDS), or an invoice not yet paid. Payments under the ₹50,000 threshold for professional fees have no TDS at all (194J threshold raised 1 Apr 2025; carried into s.393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 from 1 Apr 2026 at the same 10%/₹50,000). The tool would then report a refund that does not exist. Only the credit on the statement can come back. The 'arrived' hint also says the Annual Information Statement shows 'it', but AIS shows TDS, not amounts paid into your account (AIS help page). Salary TDS is not counted even though 'tax due on the year' includes tax on salary.

India 'comes back when you file the year's return' is unconditional, and wrong for late years. For 2025-26 income, a belated return is possible only up to 31 Dec 2026 (or before assessment is completed). An updated return 'cannot result in… increase in refund' (incometax.gov.in income-tax-returns page). The return must also be e-verified, and the refund goes only to a pre-validated account.

India has no advance-tax line and no interest. In the 'still to pay' branch there is no input for advance or self-assessment tax already paid, so the balance is overstated. When the balance is ₹10,000 or more, advance tax was due during the year (15 June, 15 Sept, 15 Dec, 15 March) and interest at 1% a month under 234B/234C can be added, so the balance is also understated. The spec shows a figure without saying either.

India 'this year' labels do not match the law. A refund is claimed for a completed year. Income from 1 Apr 2026 falls under the Income-tax Act, 2025: 'tax year' replaces assessment year, and per the department's TDS compliance page the statement for tax year 2026-27 is AIS in Form No. 168 (the Form 26AS successor). The lesson and its takeaways still say Form 26AS and AY. The tool's labels and asOf line say neither which year they follow nor which Act.

India 'missing' hint: 'It follows once the payer corrects its filing' oversimplifies. After the deductor revises, the reader may still need a revised return or a rectification request (s.155(20) of the old Act, within two years) for the credit to be given.

The India source for 'Tax due' is the wrong page. return-applicable-1 lists slabs and has no calculator. The department's calculator is incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/income-tax-calculator. It asks for the AY and compares the regimes, which is exactly the 'regime verdict' surface the spec avoids, so the hint must say to use your return's computed figure first.

The '15 January' date belongs to the next calendar year, and IRS dates move to the next business day when they fall on a weekend or holiday (gig work page, 28 Jun 2026). As of 22 Sep 2026, only 15 Jan 2027 is left for tax year 2026.

verify.lens: safety-and-scope skeptic: advice, promises, personal data, content rules, and maths edge cases (zero, negative, huge, non-integer, rate 0)
problems: US maths is wrong for large profits. selfEmploymentSetAside applies 15.3% to all of 92.35% of profit. It never caps the 12.4% Social Security part at the wage base (2026: $184,500 of combined wages and net earnings, per ssa.gov search results; IRS Topic 554 confirms the cap exists and changes each year), and it leaves out the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax above $200,000. Checked in node: a $300,000 profit gives SE $42,389, but capped it is $30,912. That overstates by $11,477, and none of the listed edge cases covers it.

The currency picker breaks the rules. Every calculator renders CurrencyField and restores lp:locale from other tools (tool-kit.tsx useLocale). A US reader whose saved locale is en-IN or en-GB would get the $400 test, the $433.14 start and the $1,000 line applied to rupees or pounds, with a 'still to pay' figure in the wrong currency. The India refund would likewise show in dollars. The spec never pins the currency.

The default example overstates tax, and that trips the estimated-tax warning. With the default 10% example income tax, the headline is '$1,207 still to pay' and the $1,000 fact fires (IRS pays four times a year). For the lesson's own person ($5,000 profit, likely a dependent), income tax is almost certainly nil. A dependent's standard deduction is the greater of $1,350 or earned income plus $450 (IRS Topic 551), and a non-dependent's is far higher. The only tax is the $707 of SE tax, which is under $1,000. The lesson's own situation line says '$707 of it is self-employment tax'. So on its opening numbers the tool tells a teen they are probably expected to pay estimated tax when they probably are not.

The $1,000 fact leaves out the exception that fits most readers. The IRS estimated taxes page says no estimated payments are needed if you had no tax liability for the prior year, were a US citizen or resident all year, and that year ran 12 months. For a first working year that usually applies. The se-tax lesson's own details carry this exception; the tool's fact does not. The fact also writes the dates as '15 April … 15 January', but the US edition and the lesson use 'April 15'.

India infers the tax withheld from the gap between fees invoiced and money paid in. That gap also holds invoices not yet paid, payments that cross 31 March, GST billed on top, platform or payment-gateway fees, and bank or currency charges on a foreign client (who deducts no TDS). The AIS page describes itself as not a complete record and has no line for unpaid invoices or fees. Any of these becomes 'Tax withheld in your name' and then a refund that 'comes back when you file'. That invents a refund the reader does not have.

India compares whole-year tax with credits from one income stream. 'Tax due on the year' covers all of the year's income, but the only credits counted are the TDS from these fees. A reader who also has salary TDS, TDS on interest or advance tax paid gets a false 'still to pay'. The mirror case exists in the US: 'Already paid or withheld this year' invites a reader to enter a W-2 job's withholding, or the Social Security and Medicare on a paycheck. The se-tax lesson says those cover that pay only. Entering them makes 'still to pay' too low, or turns it into 'more has been paid'.

The India headline reads as a promise: '₹15,000 comes back when you file the year's return'. A refund depends on e-verification, a validated bank account, the tax-due figure being right, and filing in time. For a year whose belated-return window has closed (2025-26 income: 31 December 2026, a date that is in the lesson but not in this spec), filing late does not bring it back. The India 'still to pay' also leaves out the interest charged on late tax and the ₹10,000 advance-tax line, so it can understate what is owed and gives the US edition a warning that India lacks.

A division by zero goes unhandled. shareOfProfit = tax / profit and shareOfMoneyIn = tax / moneyIn. When costs exceed money in, profit is 0, so the share is NaN, or Infinity if an income tax share exists (checked in node: [500, 900, 10, 0] gives NaN for the share of profit). When money in is 0, the share of money in is NaN. The 'US fact' line would print NaN%.

Negative inputs go unhandled, and existing islands do not guard them either. toNumber keeps '-', and the min='0' attribute is not enforced while typing. Checked in node: costs −1,000, an income-tax share of −50 and already paid −100 give a total tax of −$2,511. In India, a negative tax due inflates the refund; a negative 'missing' adds to it; a negative 'invoiced' or 'arrived' flips the ledger. The spec checks only a rate above 100, arrived above invoiced, and missing above withheld.

The $400 test contradicts the site's own teaching and is fixed in only one place. The spec applies $400 to 92.35% of profit, so tax starts at a profit of $433.14, and it corrects only the se-tax summary. The se-tax body says 'Your net earnings are your net profit … Once they reach $400'. The glossary entry net-earnings.json defines net earnings as brought in minus expenses, with no 92.35%. pricing-a-job.mdx line 182 says the same and sets aside 15.3%, not 14.13%. On a profit between $400 and $433.13, the tool would show $0 SE tax while the glossary and two lessons say it applies.

The US result ledger does not add up. 'Money in − Costs = Net profit $5,000' is followed in the same ledger by '+ SE $707 + Income tax $500 = Tax for the year $1,207'. Read as one ledger, the $5,000 sits above a total that leaves it out, which breaks the DESIGN.md rule that calculator results are 'a ledger whose rows add up'. 'Tax for the year' and the headline also present an example rate as the year's tax.

The 'US fact: 24.1% of profit and 20.1% of money in' reads like an effective tax rate, but about 10 points of it are the reader's example rate. It invites comparison with real rates as though it were a finding.

The spec depends on infrastructure that does not exist. It relies on 'Rules in regions.ts … with asOf' and 'the 12-month test'. grep finds no Rule type, no asOf field and no staleness test anywhere in src/, tests/ or scripts/. The effort estimate leaves out building them, so the claimed guard against stale constants is not in place.

A source link does not match its field. The India 'Tax due on the year … or the department's calculator' input links to return-applicable-1, a page about which ITR form applies, not the calculator. The department's Income and Tax Calculator (incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/income-tax-calculator) exists and has a business-or-profession field.

Real income can end up in a link. This tool takes real income, tax and credits, and the shared ToolActions puts every input into the copied or shared URL's query string. On shared phones (18% of Indians use someone else's device, according to REGIONAL_TEACHING), a shared link and the browser history carry the reader's own income and tax figures. The spec says nothing about it.
fixes: In finance.ts: seTax = round(min(counted, rules.ssWageBase) × 0.124 + counted × 0.029). Add rules.ssWageBase = 184500 (asOf 2026, source ssa.gov) to the US Rules. The SideIncomeTax island does not render CurrencyField and does not call useLocale. It formats with the edition's fixed locale (India en-IN/INR, US en-US/USD) passed from [tool].astro. Add an e2e test that sets lp:locale=en-IN, loads /us/tools/side-income-tax, and expects '$'.

Set the US default incomeTaxPercent to '0' and relabel the field 'Income tax, % of profit, if any (an example)'. Add a fact from Rules: 'For 2025-26 income, a belated return can be filed until 31 December 2026' (asOf, linked to the income-tax-returns help page). Still-to-pay sentence: 'at least ₹X still to pay; interest is added to tax paid late'. Link incometax.gov.in advance tax and interest help.

Show the percentage facts only when profit > 0 and moneyIn > 0. When profit = 0, show only the loss sentence and hide both shares. Unit test [500, 900, 10, 0] and [0, 0, 10, 0] and assert no NaN or Infinity is rendered.

Give every money field and every percentage field an error when the value is below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Exclude any field in error from the sum and show no result until it is fixed. Add unit tests for negative costs, rate, already paid, tax due, TDS and missing credit.

In the same commit, also fix the se-tax body ('Your net earnings are 92.35% of your net profit … once they reach $400, about $433 of profit'), the glossary net-earnings.json definition and example, the self-employment-tax.json wording, and the pricing-a-job.mdx body line 182 and its details and quiz 'why' text. Ledger 2 under the heading 'Tax on it': SE tax (15.3% of $4,618, which is 92.35% of $5,000), + income tax at your example rate, = tax on these figures, − estimated tax already paid, = still to pay, closed with a double rule. Show the $4,618 base as a caption, not as a row.
Drop the combined 24.1% and 20.1% fact. Keep only 'Self-employment tax is 14.1% of profit, set by law', and when the example rate is above 0, add 'plus your example X%'.

Add to the effort estimate and the file list: a Rule { value: number; source: Source; asOf: string } interface in regions.ts; the US rules seRate, seBase, seThreshold, estimatedTaxLine, ssWageBase and additionalMedicareThreshold, and the India rule belatedReturnDate; and a unit test that fails when any asOf is more than 12 months before the build date.

For this tool, put a privacy line above the copy and share buttons: 'The link carries the figures you typed. Share it only if you are happy for others to see them.' Or pass an option to ToolActions that leaves the income and tax fields out of the link.

The content-legal judge would build it only under three conditions: return claims appear solely on screens marked as made-up fakes, the market-signal test exemption is scoped to those lines, and no security, index or price appears anywhere. The engineering judge rejected it for weakening the SEBI guardrail. Because both judges did not rank it, it waits. No EU lesson teaches revolving card balances, and minimum rules differ by country.

A US payment-app scam set (the FTC reports a $380 median loss on payment-app scams) waits for a US lesson. Then add 'us' to spot-the-fake's regions with a bank.
Country presets for take-home pay, one country at a time, each with sourced, dated rates, a reviewer and tests. The generic typed-amount version ships first.
A 'year so far' row on take-home pay (India TDS against tax due; a US W-2 against the return), once the tax-due figure can be linked to the official calculators.
India advance-tax instalments as a final block of side-income-tax, once an India lesson teaches advance tax. Most readers fall under the ₹10,000 threshold.
US only. It needs dated per-year rates, verification of the capitalisation rule after 1 July 2026, and a lesson. The monthly-payment question is already answered by the loan tool.
The arithmetic is sound (NGPF Bummer), but no lesson teaches deductibles or co-pays yet.

Printable worksheets of each tool's example for Business Lab clubs (PROJECT_BRIEF v2 teacher kit), after the tools settle.

rejected.why: Both judges rejected it. It sets borrowing routes side by side for a minor ('a lending app … the card … wait for payday'). Even unranked they read as 'which is better', and the ₹0 'wait' row is an implicit winner. It puts a lending app in front of the reader as a way to cover a gap, runs close to the SPENT backfire LEARNING_DESIGN warns about, is medium-large to build, and depends on another tool. buffer-target answers the buffer question with one ceil().

Proposal 1's simulation scripts an 'add one more purchase' step to end in a shortfall and a fee: a consequence-of-spending design that can moralise. It needs day windows, predict-then-open steps and a static fallback. pay-later-payday teaches the same sum on the reader's own plans at about a third of the build.

Brokerage and F&O margin tools are trading aids for a documented harm: under-30s were 43% of F&O traders in FY26, and 89% of them lost money (SEBI).

'Should I buy it?', 'Pay down debt, save or invest?' and 'Do I have too much debt?' (Bank of America, Practical Money Skills) are named for the reader's decision and output a recommendation, which the education-not-advice rule bars.

Scoring minors' financial well-being is sensitive, its norms are adult, and its feedback (fund sizes, cover amounts) is advice.
Shady Sam-style games reward manipulation, ask for a name, ship heavy bundles and load third-party analytics. Only their pressure-line cues carry over, into job-offer-check's reveals.
'Three cuts, one year' and lunch trackers (Chase, Practical Money Skills, Finanzas para todos) moralise through their defaults (eating out, smoking), and no lesson teaches them.
'Impact of 1%' and cost-of-delay tools need an expected-return assumption next to investing, where the SEBI education rule and the no-returns rule make every default risky.
A 'save ₹X' comparison gives a verdict. yearly-rate already covers flat offers: type the printed instalment.
A single division that invites gaming a score against a '30%' guideline that needs careful sourcing. If anything, it belongs as an explorable in the credit-file lesson.
It needs dated HICP weight tables for each country and 12 spending categories, which is too large for a small tool, and no lesson teaches it.
Small value for readers far below the registration thresholds. It fits as a line in the pricing-abroad lesson.
The HRA exemption applies only under the old regime, gratuity is one line of take-home-pay's hint, and an EPF corpus is a 40-year projection. None of them is a first earner's question.

summaryForOwner: Three proposals were researched from the free tools at Chase, Bank of America, NerdWallet, Bankrate, the CFPB, NGPF and Indian and European public sites, and two reviewers checked them against the site's rules and its code. Nine tools are to be built now. That takes India to 12 tools and Europe and the United States to 11 each, and every tool opens on the numbers from a lesson that already teaches it. Take-home pay turns a payslip into what reaches your account, line by line. Buffer target says on which payday a buffer for your must-pay costs is ready. Card minimum shows how long a card takes to clear at the minimum payment and what that costs. Yearly rate (India only) turns a fee or an instalment plan into a yearly rate. Pay-later plans (Europe and the US) shows what one payday has left after the instalments, and rent share (Europe) sets rent and bills against net pay and Eurostat's 40% line, with the cost of moving in. Tax on side income works out US self-employment tax and an example income tax set-aside, and in India what comes back from tax withheld on fees; it never works out income tax slabs. Two drills of made-up screens are added: 'spot the fake' gets a Europe edition built on the name check banks now run before a transfer, and a new job-offer drill runs in all three editions, each with ordinary cases so refusing everything is not the answer. Pricing a job from its hours and a money-tips drill are held for a later batch, and ideas such as a 'surprise cost' simulator, a credit-score sandbox, tax-regime and trading calculators and any 'which is better' tool were turned down because they rank choices, invent numbers or read as advice. The tools page will be grouped by life moment, a copied link will carry numbers after a # so they never reach a server, and several lessons will point to their new tools (the se-tax lesson summary also needs one wording fix); nothing will be pushed or deployed without you.
